solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: For whom one might provide perfect meal? (8)

annotation.definition: For whom one might provide perfect meal?

blocks.note: the surface reads 'one' as a cook or host; the setter means 'one' is the person who provides the meal by being it
the question mark warns that the meal is a person, and the diner is someone who eats people

annotation.surface: A host wonders which guest would most appreciate a perfect dinner.
annotation.walkthrough: Read 'one might provide' as cooking for someone and nothing is cryptic; read it as 'one might BE the meal provided' and only a cannibal fits.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: to a people-eater, any person ('one') is the ideal meal, so the whole clue defines the diner.

entries.clue: Fashionable way to make a Martini? (4,2)

blocks.note: an informal phrase for trendy, up to date
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in the bar order gin and It

annotation.surface: A trendy barman explains the stylish way to mix a Martini.
annotation.walkthrough: IT is short for Italian vermouth, as in the old British bar order 'gin and It'; a Martini is gin made WITH IT.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the dated slang for up to date, and literally mixing gin with It, the Italian vermouth in a Martini.

entries.clue: English atheist wrong to hang back (8)

indicatorNotes.wrong: the letters are put together wrongly, so rearrange them

annotation.surface: An English unbeliever is thought mistaken for holding back from something.
annotation.walkthrough: Read 'English atheist' as one person in the surface, but it splits into E plus the seven letters of ATHEIST to be rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe pausing, reluctant to act, and the verb swaps straight into 'to hang back'.

entries.clue: Learn from the archdeacon (4)

indicatorNotes.from: the answer is taken out from the words that follow

annotation.surface: A cleric passes on news learned from a senior churchman.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer spans the gap between two words: the end of 'the' and the start of 'archdeacon'.
annotation.definitionFit: The 'find out' sense, as in 'I hear you've moved', where being told is learning.

entries.clue: Pest made off in a rush (8)

indicatorNotes.off: the letters go off, out of their order

annotation.surface: A nuisance of a person dashes away in a hurry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Made off' looks like a phrasal verb meaning fled; split it and 'made' is fodder while 'off' does the rearranging.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun synonym: a headlong rush of cattle or a panicking crowd.

entries.clue: Office worker briefly allowed place of worship (6)

indicatorNotes.briefly: cut short, so the last letter of the word goes

blocks.note: a temporary worker from an agency

annotation.surface: A temporary office worker is permitted some time at a church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' sits before 'allowed' and shortens it, not the time the worker is given.
annotation.definitionFit: A general term covering the building of many faiths, Hindu, Jewish or ancient Greek.

entries.clue: Sharp smell of insect rising (4)

indicatorNotes.rising: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top

annotation.surface: Something pungent wafts off a swarm of flying insects.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rising' works because this is a down clue: an upward reading turns GNAT round.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, used of both smells and tastes, like the tang of sea air.

entries.clue: US state welcoming Republican soldier (6)

indicatorNotes.welcoming: the state takes the letter in, as a host welcomes a guest

annotation.surface: A New England state gives a warm reception to a GOP soldier.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pairs the state with a soldier, but the soldier is the definition and the state is only the outside shell.
annotation.definitionFit: A marine is a soldier who serves at sea with a navy, so the general word fits.

entries.clue: Nearly everyone preparing for war is frightening (8)

indicatorNotes.Nearly: not quite all of the word, so its last letter goes

annotation.surface: Almost the whole nation readying itself for conflict is a scary prospect.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a sentence whose last word is the definition, with 'is' joining it to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain adjective synonym: both describe what causes fear or alarm.

entries.clue: Make very slow progress in church (4)

annotation.surface: A congregation shuffles slowly up the aisle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word placing the progress inside a church, but it is a piece of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: The verb from the unit of length: to move forward a tiny distance at a time.

entries.clue: Friend in city across the pond quietly heading west (3)

indicatorNotes.heading west: in an across entry, west is leftward, so read right to left

blocks.note: LA = Los Angeles; 'across the pond' means in America

annotation.surface: A friend living in an American city moves quietly westward.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Across the pond' is British slang for the United States, the Atlantic being the pond.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal synonym for a friend or mate.

entries.clue: Clumsy bishop locates impediment (8)

indicatorNotes.Clumsy: the letters are handled clumsily and fall out of order

blocks.note: B = bishop, as in chess notation

annotation.surface: An awkward churchman finally finds what is in his way.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Locates' reads as the verb joining wordplay to definition, but it is fodder; the definition is simply the last word.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain noun synonym: anything that blocks the way forward.

entries.clue: University caterer cooking chicken? (8)

indicatorNotes.cooking: the letters are cooked, stirred into a new form

annotation.surface: A college caterer is busy roasting chicken for the dining hall.
annotation.walkthrough: The kitchen surface makes chicken food, but here it is a living animal; the question mark says a chicken is just one example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a chicken is one kind of living being, flagged by the question mark.

entries.clue: Almost get rid of Times (4)

indicatorNotes.Almost: not quite the whole word, so its last letter goes

blocks.note: ERASE (get rid of) without its last letter

annotation.surface: Someone nearly scraps their subscription to the Times newspaper.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital T disguises 'Times' as the newspaper; capitals may mislead, and here it is plain periods of history.
annotation.definitionFit: A plural synonym for periods of history, as in 'in Victorian times'.

entries.clue: Dislike author’s initial adaptation (8)

indicatorNotes.initial: the initial of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a new form of a work, such as a film of a novel

annotation.surface: A writer hates the first attempt at turning their book into a film.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dislike' reads as a verb in the surface, but the answer is the noun, a strong dislike.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun synonym: a strong feeling of dislike or distaste.

entries.clue: Fat female dog (4)

annotation.surface: An overweight bitch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fat female dog' reads as one overweight animal, but the adjective is the definition, standing for a noun.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal noun for fat, meaning the soft loose kind that wobbles on the body.

entries.clue: Bet on the French acquiring European vehicle (6)

indicatorNotes.acquiring: BET takes in the letter, acquiring it
indicatorNotes.on: in a down entry, one piece written on another follows it

annotation.surface: A gambler wagers on French rivals picking up a European car.
annotation.walkthrough: The Volkswagen Beetle is the classic German car, so 'European vehicle' seems one idea; 'European' only supplies E.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by type: the Volkswagen car of that name, nicknamed for its rounded shape.

entries.clue: Very happy to catch EV up (8)

indicatorNotes.to catch: ELATED catches EV and holds it inside

annotation.surface: An electric-vehicle owner is thrilled to catch up with another EV.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Catch up' looks like one phrase; split it and 'up' is the definition at the end.
annotation.definitionFit: Raised to a height, the sense of up in 'the platform is up off the ground'.

entries.clue: Tempt a couple of learners to go on river (6)

indicatorNotes.to go on: in a down entry, the first pieces go on top of the river

blocks.note: the Ure, a river in Yorkshire

annotation.surface: Two driving pupils are lured into a boating trip.
annotation.walkthrough: L for learner comes from the L-plates British learner drivers display. The Ure is a Yorkshire river, a crossword regular.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: to entice someone with something attractive, as a lure draws fish.

entries.clue: When one might expect to receive letter from Athens? (3)

annotation.definition: When one might expect to receive

blocks.clueFragment: When one might expect to receive
blocks.note: the abbreviation for the estimated time of arrival
a letter of the Greek alphabet

annotation.surface: Someone wonders when a letter posted in Athens will arrive.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about post, but the 'letter' is an alphabet letter, and the first half describes the time a delivery is due.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the estimated time of arrival tells you when to expect something, and eta is the seventh Greek letter.

entries.clue: Dartmoor cave providing cover for hunter (4)

indicatorNotes.providing cover for: the words cover the answer, which lies inside them

annotation.surface: A cave on the moor gives a hunter somewhere to hide.
annotation.walkthrough: Dartmoor is a moorland in Devon, so a hunter sheltering there sounds natural; the hunter is actually a sea creature.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the killer whale is a top predator of the ocean.

entries.clue: Reportedly remitted money to America (4)

indicatorNotes.Reportedly: as reported, spoken, so the sound counts, not the spelling

annotation.surface: Someone is said to have wired funds to the United States.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Money to America' is the definition read as 'money, to an American': a cent is a US coin.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example with a regional tag: a coin in American money, one hundredth of a dollar.

entries.clue: Fail nothing in London School of Economics (4)

indicatorNotes.in: the letter goes in the abbreviation

annotation.surface: A student at the London School of Economics fails with zero marks.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface places a failure at the college; in the wordplay the college initials simply wrap the zero.
annotation.definitionFit: An intransitive verb sense: to fail to win, as a team does when it loses.

entries.clue: Puritan concealing rubbish project (8)

indicatorNotes.concealing: PRUDE conceals the rubbish inside itself

blocks.note: a prim, strait-laced person, around ROT after its P

annotation.surface: A prim moralist hides a worthless scheme.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Project' sits at the end looking like a noun, a scheme; it is the verb, to stick out.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb synonym, with project said pro-JECT: to jut out beyond a surface.

entries.clue: Strict new school in the East End (6)

indicatorNotes.in the East End: Cockneys of London's East End drop the H from the start of words

blocks.note: HARROW, a famous English boarding school, with the H dropped

annotation.surface: A newly founded school in the East of London is run on strict lines.
annotation.walkthrough: Harrow is a famous English private school; the East End is working-class London, whose Cockney speakers traditionally drop H, so Harrow becomes 'Arrow.
annotation.definitionFit: The limited, rigid sense, as in a narrow interpretation of a rule.

entries.clue: Vulgar soldiers head for the lowest level (8)

indicatorNotes.head for: the head of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: Rough troops march down to the bottom floor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Head for' reads as a verb of movement, so the soldiers seem to be heading downstairs; it takes the first letter of 'the'.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: the floor of a building below ground, beneath all the others.
